# Conclusion

This study used OrientDB and Jupyter Notebooks to analyze how GitHub repositories popularity relates to development activity and
how activity varies by language for the 200 most popular repositories. For the first hypothesis, the data does not support
the idea that more stars imply higher activity. Within the top 200 repositories, projects with very different star counts often show
similar activity level. Stars alone are therefore not a reliable indicator of how actively a project is maintained. The second hypothesis,
that activity differs by primary language, is clearly supported.

This study has several limitations. Most importantly, the dataset is small and biased towards the most popular repositories.
Many practically relevant libraries likely sit in a mid-range of roughly 1000-50000 stars and are not covered here. In addition,
activity is approximated only by their average merged pull requests over a time span, ignoring other signals such as issues,
commits, releases or project age. Future work could extend this approach to a larger and more representative sample of repositories
and refine the activity metric.
